$comment: Catalog for `vshell mise`, `vshell agent` and `vshell dev-env`. One list
feeds the ~/.local/bin stubs, the default-agent picker, the Developer
settings tab and the VGS menu; nothing else may carry its own copy.
agents: coding-agent harnesses. `package` is what mise installs, `command`
the stub name in ~/.local/bin, `bin` the executable inside the package
(defaults to command). `launch` is the argv the default-agent launcher runs,
the agent's own spelling of "do not stop to ask".
`exec` is a path under the mise install root that the stub and the launcher
run directly, for a package whose own directory must never go on PATH. The
Cursor Agent package ships `node` and `rg` beside its binary, and mise's
directory sits ahead of /usr/bin, so exporting it replaces both system
commands for every process the session starts. Such an entry passes an
empty mise `bin_path=`, which moves the export to the install root, and
the two go together: `mise x` then finds nothing of the tool's name inside
the package and falls through to PATH, where the stub itself answers.
`icon` is `nerd:<hex>` (bundled Nerd Font) or `brand:<hex>` (bundled
omarchy brand marks); `color` is the brand's dominant color for the
launcher tile. Every launchable entry and every env carries one: without
it the tile falls back to the theme grey and reads as unbranded beside
the rest. A mark that is monochrome takes that mark's own near-white.
apps: developer applications. Same launcher, install and removal as an
agent, and the same icon and colour fields; they are apart because an app
is not a coding agent and every surface says which it is. `kind: gui`
launches detached with no terminal around it.
`buildEnv` holds variables the install needs and the tool must not inherit
-- Hermes pins its interpreter with `UV_PYTHON`, which would otherwise
resolve that version in the user's own projects too, so the stub drops it
again before it execs. `requires` are mise packages the backend itself
needs first. `present` is a path under the install proving the build
honoured that environment; without it `mise up` would rebuild the tool
against whatever interpreter was to hand and nothing would notice.
`arch` lists the machine architectures an entry publishes builds for.
Absent means every one. VGS ships aarch64, so an entry that only builds
x86_64 has to say so: without it an ARM owner gets a tile whose first
install has no asset to choose.
A `package` may carry mise backend options in brackets: `matching_regex`
picks the release asset when the platform matcher cannot, `rename_exe`
gives it a name that does not change with the version. cmux publishes only
a `nightly` tag, so its package names it; mise then sees no new version and
the app updates itself.
`channels` lets the owner pick which release stream an entry installs from.
`options` maps a channel id to the backend options that select it, merged
into the entry's own bracket list; an empty string is the package
unchanged. `default` names the stream used until the owner chooses, and
`vshell mise channel <id> <channel>` records the choice. Only an entry
whose prereleases are the same product gets channels: Orca's are a
different application, and cmux publishes no stable tag to choose against.
tools: developer CLIs that get a lazy stub but are not agents. They
carry an id and a name so the Developer tab can list them and act on
one, and no icon or colour because nothing launches them from a tile.
envs: language environments. `tools` are mise packages installed globally;
`installer` names a non-mise route the helper implements; `managedBy` names
a command whose presence at a distribution path means the package manager
owns the environment and VGS neither installs nor removes it; `packages` are
distribution packages (keyed by dependencies.json distro ids) installed
first; `present` is the path whose existence means installed.
